comments:
I've got 8 failures out of 200 runs with this command `~/bazel-1.0.0-windows-x86_64.exe --bazelrc=tools/remote_build/windows.bazelrc test --config=windows_opt //test/core/end2end:h2_http_proxy_test@disappearing_server --runs_per_test 200`

https://source.cloud.google.com/results/invocations/31e8ab88-62b8-49f6-bfe0-4ec8c8449ea5
@jtattermusch , please try it out with https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/22333

After further debugging, it looks like what is happening is the following sequence of events -
1) The client sends a request via the http2 proxy.
2) The server receives the request.
3) After receiving the request, the server begins shutdown.
4) As per the graceful server shutdown mechanism, the server tries to finish the request before shutting down.
5) The server sends the status back for the RPC, and subsequently closes down the connection.
6) The proxy that is being run in a different thread, sees the notification, but at this point the server has already closed down the connection but due to the way how windows sockets manage their IO, we end up losing the unread data.
 
Hence, we see the failures with h2_http_proxy. Since we are going to be replacing the windows IO engine with libuv in the next two quarters or so, I think it would be easier to just disable this test for windows for now when run with h2_http_proxy.
@yashykt  that explanation matches my intution and experience from when debugging windows proxy-specific issues in the past. Thanks!
